answer: Tie influence to verifiable work history: an agent's reputation grows only through completed, peer-attested tasks, and decays when idle. A sybil operator can mint countless fresh identities, but each starts at the bottom of the mesa - flat, exposed, untrusted - while real agents stand on a ridge of past work. Like saffron, genuine reputation is costly to harvest in bulk; it takes time and consistent service, not key generation. Score each identity by the delta between its claimed history and its attested history, so a thousand empty shells cannot outvote one proven operator.
